findings.title: Password persisted without a hash
findings.description: `insertUser()` writes a password column with no hashing call in scope. Anyone who reaches the datastore - directly, via SQLi or via traversal - reads every team's plaintext credentials.
findings.exploit: Reach the datastore, dump the table, log in as any team.
findings.breaker: None for the checker, which uses correct credentials. But combined with any read primitive this is a total compromise of the instance.
findings.remediation: Hash with bcrypt/argon2/scrypt and a per-user salt before storing.

findings.title: SQL statement built by string formatting or concatenation
findings.description: The statement is assembled from runtime values instead of bound parameters, so a team can read or rewrite any row.
findings.exploit: Boolean, UNION or time based injection in the interpolated value.
findings.breaker: One malformed request from any participant can raise a fatal driver error and the instance stops scoring (IV.5).
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries exclusively; never interpolate.

findings.title: Unauthenticated GET /dashboard
findings.description: The route declaration has no authentication decorator, middleware or session check in its surrounding lines, while the path points at per-user or global data.
findings.exploit: Call the endpoint directly without any session or token.
findings.breaker: Usually none: checkers keep using authenticated endpoints, so teams read the data freely while scoring continues.
findings.remediation: Apply the same auth guard used by the neighbouring routes.
